messages:
kevin: quick heads-up — saw a p99 jump on /chat-stream after switching kernel -> int8-kv-optim. console card shows p50/p95/p99 but no token-level waterfall so unclear if KV misses or kernel overhead.

sophia: ugh. do you have the numbers? throughput + error rate?

kevin: p50 45ms, p95 220ms, p99 760ms. throughput ~850 rps (aggregate), error rate 0.3% (grpc timeouts). I captured a short profile from the pod:

```
# perf top snapshot (simplified)
kernel_loop          42%  (attention kernel int8 path)
kv_cache_miss        18%
rpc_serialization    12%
batching_overhead    10%
other                18%
```

maria: thanks. that kernel_loop number points at kernel selection, but kv_cache_miss 18% is non-trivial. what was the average sequence length? long context can push more KV churn.

kevin: avg seq len ~320 tokens for this route (chat-stream uses long context + system prompts). KV hit rate from the pod was ~82% (measured via the runtime trace).

jon: it sounds like two possible levers: 1) prefer a kernel variant with better int8 KV handling for longer contexts, or 2) change batching heuristics to avoid head-of-line stalls for sequences with big KV state. we should be careful since prefer-variant might increase per-token cost.

perf-bot: [alert] route=/chat-stream p99=760ms > 700ms for 5m window. triggered at 1951234567.

infra-bot: deploy of kernel int8-kv-optim rolled out to dedicated pool at 1951234540. rollback option: /ops/kernels/int8-kv-optim -> previous int8-default.

sophia: can we add token-level latency breakdown to the route KPI card? even a lightweight stacked bar (KV read, kernel exec, network, serialization) would make triage much faster.

maria: agreed. current console signal has p50/p95/p99 but not per-token slices. proposing: add new per-route metric: token_latency_partitioned with buckets: kv_hit, kv_miss, kernel_exec, io, serial. visual: small stacked waterfall + p50/p95/p99 markers.

kevin: prototype query I used (pseudo-metric-dsl):
```
select
  route,
  histogram(token_latency_ms, buckets=[0,1,5,10,50,100,200,500,1000]) by component
from runtime.tokens
where route = '/chat-stream' and ts >= now()-5m
```

jon: that looks good. two ops questions: 1) sampling — we shouldn't ingest every token at full fidelity for high-throughput routes. maybe 1% tokens + adaptive sampling for p99. 2) storage/retention — keep high-fidelity traces for 1h, then summary histograms.

maria: exactly. sampling rules: default 0.5% tokens per route, escalate to 5% on p95 or error spikes for 10m. rollout via console config UI (per-route).

sophia: also want an attribution column: kernel_variant and kv_hit_rate per-bucket so dashboard can filter to see if a kernel variant causes higher kernel_exec time.

kevin: agree. from the profile, kernel choice correlates with kernel_loop time. adding variant label would let us pivot quickly.

jon: action items:
- kevin: attach the pod flamegraph and raw profile to the incident ticket (GH #4521).
- maria: sketch dashboard mock (waterfall + sampling config) and add to console roadmap.
- sophia: add metric ingestion proposal (sampling + escalation) to observability RFC.
- infra: add a temporary rule to revert int8-kv-optim -> int8-default if p99 > 700ms for 15m.

kevin: noted. attaching minimal flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/reports/1951234567-flame

maria: mock will include: p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rate, token-waterfall breakdown, kernel_variant selector, kv_hit_rate sparkline, and a quick 'rerun query' button that pulls 5m window.

sophia: thanks — once we have the waterfall on the card triage should be way faster. tagging @jon for follow-up on sampling limits and @infra-bot to watch the revert rule. :thumbsup:

jon: I'll draft the sampling text this afternoon. if anyone sees new alerts push them to GH #4521 so we keep all artifacts in one place.

perf-bot: note: escalation policy triggered -> oncall paged if p99 > 900ms for 10m. current p99 760ms so not escalated.

kevin: closing loop — I rolled the int8-kv-optim back to int8-default on the dedicated pool at 1951234585. p99 dropped back to ~190ms within 30s. will follow up with a controlled perf test matrix comparing kernels across seq len and kv-hit rates.

maria: lovely. once you have the test matrix we can add recommended kernel selection rules to the console (auto-suggest).
